security_audit.summary: This is a benign meta-skill for authoring and validating Claude Skills. After manual review of all 30 static findings, every one was adjudicated a false positive: the flagged 'backtick execution' matches are markdown backtick literals in documentation, the 'path traversal' matches are ordinary relative paths (../assets, ../SKILL.md links), and the shell command substitutions are safe, standard bash idioms with no untrusted input, no eval, and no network access. No semantic threats were found. SKILL.md is flagged for manual review only because its leading 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line prevents automatic frontmatter parsing.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md begins with a 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' prefix line before the YAML frontmatter, which prevents automated frontmatter parsing and left the file unscanned.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the leading 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line so SKILL.md starts with the '---' frontmatter delimiter on line 1, matching the skill's own validate-skill.sh requirement.

content.user_title: Build reliable Claude Skills from your docs
content.value_statement: Turning scattered documentation, APIs, and code into a well-structured Claude Skill is slow and error-prone, and skills that misfire or dump raw docs waste effort. This meta-skill gives you templates, a scaffolding generator, a spec validator, and a quality gate so every skill you build activates reliably and reads like an operator's manual.
actual_capabilities: Scaffolds a new skill directory (SKILL.md, references, scripts, assets) using create-skill.sh in minimal or full mode
Validates SKILL.md frontmatter, required sections, and structure with validate-skill.sh, including a strict mode
Provides minimal and complete SKILL.md templates for quick bootstrapping or production-grade skills
Defines a decidable quality gate and scoring checklist for pre-delivery review
Guides refactoring of long or unclear skills by splitting content into a navigable references/ directory
limitations: The validator is heuristic; strict mode assumes the recommended section headings and may not fit unusual layouts
It builds skills but is not itself a domain skill, so it provides no domain-specific knowledge
The shell scripts require bash and common POSIX tools (awk, sed, grep, find) and are not designed for Windows CMD or PowerShell
It cannot verify external facts; authors must supply accurate source material and verification paths

use_cases.title: Create a new skill from documentation
use_cases.description: Scaffold a skill directory, write decidable activation triggers, extract a Quick Reference, and add reproducible examples from official docs and code samples.
use_cases.target_user: Developers packaging internal or open-source docs into a reusable Claude Skill

use_cases.title: Refactor a doc-dump skill
use_cases.description: Split a bloated SKILL.md into short copy-paste patterns plus a references/ directory, and add boundaries to stop the skill from misfiring.
use_cases.target_user: Skill maintainers cleaning up an existing skill that is too long or unreliable

use_cases.title: Enforce a quality gate before shipping
use_cases.description: Run the validator in strict mode and the scoring checklist so every skill meets a consistent bar before it is published to a team or marketplace.
use_cases.target_user: Team leads standardizing skill quality across many contributors

prompt_templates.title: Bootstrap a new skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the claude-skills meta-skill to scaffold a new skill named my-api. Generate the full directory layout and fill in the SKILL.md frontmatter with a decidable description.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a brand-new skill from scratch

prompt_templates.title: Extract a Quick Reference
prompt_templates.prompt: I have these API docs. Using the claude-skills meta-skill, pull out the 10 to 20 most common patterns and write them as a short, copy-paste Quick Reference section.
prompt_templates.scenario: Condensing large source material into usable patterns

prompt_templates.title: Refactor an existing skill
prompt_templates.prompt: My SKILL.md has become a long documentation dump. Apply the claude-skills meta-skill to move long-form text into references/, rewrite the Quick Reference, and add a Not For / Boundaries section.

prompt_templates.title: Run the full quality gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate skills/my-skill with the claude-skills meta-skill in strict mode, then score it against the quality checklist and list every issue I must fix before shipping.
prompt_templates.scenario: Final pre-delivery review with the validator and rubric

output_examples.input: Scaffold a full skill named postgresql into the skills directory.
output_examples.output: A new skills/postgresql directory is created containing SKILL.md, a references folder with index.md and starter docs, plus empty scripts and assets folders, followed by next-step guidance for editing the entrypoint.

The validator checks the frontmatter name and description, confirms the required section headings, verifies references/index.md exists, and reports any missing sections or an insufficient example count as errors to fix.

best_practices: Write the frontmatter description as what plus when, with concrete trigger keywords, so activation stays decidable.
Keep the Quick Reference to short, directly usable patterns and move anything needing paragraphs of explanation into references/.
Always include a Not For / Boundaries section and at least three reproducible examples before shipping.
anti_patterns: Pasting raw documentation into SKILL.md instead of extracting short patterns and moving long-form text into references/.
Writing a vague description like helps with X, which makes the skill activate unreliably or not at all.
Skipping the boundaries section, which causes the skill to misfire on tasks it was never meant to handle.

faq.question: What does this skill actually do?
faq.answer: It helps you build and refactor Claude Skills. It provides templates, a scaffolding script, a validator, and a quality checklist so your skills are well-structured and activate reliably.

faq.question: Do the included scripts need internet access?
faq.answer: No. The create-skill.sh and validate-skill.sh scripts depend only on bash and common POSIX tools such as awk, sed, and grep. They perform no network requests.

faq.question: Is this a domain skill for a specific technology?
faq.answer: No. It is a meta-skill for building other skills. Domain-specific knowledge belongs in the skills you create with it, not in this one.

faq.question: What is the difference between minimal and full mode?
faq.answer: Minimal mode generates just the core SKILL.md and index. Full mode also creates starter reference documents such as getting started, API, examples, and troubleshooting files.

faq.question: What does strict mode in the validator check?
faq.answer: Strict mode enforces the recommended section headings, requires the frontmatter name to match the directory name, requires references/index.md when a references folder exists, and requires at least three examples.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to run?
faq.answer: Yes. Security review found no dangerous behavior. The shell scripts only read local files, parse text, and write template files locally, with no network access and no execution of untrusted input.
